# bronto_group (Resource)

Manages a Bronto user group.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "bronto_group" "platform" {
  name        = "Platform Team"
  description = "Owns core platform infrastructure"

  # Optional: reconciled via individual add/remove membership API calls,
  # not the group's own create/update endpoints.
  members = [
    {
      member_type = "USER"
      member_id   = bronto_user.alice.id
    },
    {
      member_type = "GROUP"
      member_id   = "02bd4c9a-e839-4fc1-b1b4-7490a1f354e7"
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The display name of the group

### Optional

- `description` (String) A brief summary or explanation of the group's purpose
- `members` (Attributes List) Users or groups that belong to this group. Reconciled via individual add/remove API calls, not the group's own create/update endpoints, so each changed member costs a separate request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--members))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number) The timestamp when the group was created, in epoch milliseconds
- `id` (String) The unique identifier for the group
- `modified_at` (Number) The timestamp when the group was last modified, in epoch milliseconds

<a id="nestedatt--members"></a>
### Nested Schema for `members`

Required:

- `member_id` (String) The id of the user or group that is a member of this group
- `member_type` (String) The kind of entity this member is: `USER` or `GROUP`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Groups can be imported by their unique ID.
terraform import bronto_group.platform 02bd4c9a-e839-4fc1-b1b4-7490a1f354e7

# Alternatively, the Bronto API can generate a ready-to-paste bronto_group
# block (including its own `import` block) for an existing group directly:
#   GET /groups/{groupId}/export?format=terraform
```
